newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dollar rise spurs German import prices in January.
newsitem.headline: Dollar rise spurs German import prices in January.

text.p: The strong rise in the dollar against the Deutschmark over the past few months has spurred a sharp increase in German import prices, data released on Tuesday by the Federal Statistics Office showed.
German import prices rose 1.0 percent in January from December to stand 2.6 percent higher than a year earlier. The January import price index rose to 100.0 from 99.0 in December.
This marks the strongest increase since May 1991, when the import price index rose 2.7 percent from a year earlier.
"In this context it should be noted that the exchange rate of the dollar against the mark was 9.8 percent higher than a year ago," the statistics office said in a statement.
An official from the statistics office also said that a strong increase in oil prices could have played a role in driving import prices higher.

Excluding oil and petroleum products, import prices rose 0.9 percent in January from December and were up 0.6 percent from a year earlier. In December, import prices had risen 0.8 percent from the previous month and were up 2.0 percent from a year earlier.

Export prices rose 0.4 percent in January from December and were up 0.5 percent from a year earlier. The index stood at 103.9 in January. Export prices had risen 0.1 percent in December from the previous months and were up 0.3 percent from the previous year.
